rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-season greenhouse experiment (2024) on red clay soil in Changsha with subsurface drip irrigation at three dissolved-oxygen levels of micro-nano bubble water x three biochar rates plus a control, three replicates. Q2: Section 3.6 and Fig. 9 - cucumber yield rose significantly as DO concentration in MNBW increased (P<0.05); average yield of treatments 1.72-44.23% above CK; IWUE and WUE also increased with DO; vitamin C and sugar-acid ratio rose and organic acid fell with DO (quality). Q4: Section 3.1/Fig. 3 - DO in MNBW significantly raised soil oxygen content and redox potential; Section 3.4/Fig. 7 - net photosynthetic rate rose with DO; Section 3.7/Fig. 10 - yield positively correlated with soil oxygen, aeration porosity and Pn.
rows.notes: Yield measured by harvest weighing only (one method). The CK (unaerated, no biochar) comparison is confounded with biochar because all non-CK treatments received biochar, but the DO main effect across biochar levels supports the aeration-vs-conventional claim. Single site, single soil, single crop, plot scale. No stated limitations beyond 'more research'; no dispersion statistics reported in text (letter groupings and ranges across treatments only). The pesticide part of the passage is not addressed by this study (see pest_control row).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own two-season greenhouse experiment with micro-nano aerated subsurface drip irrigation and biochar on cucumber.
rows.notes: The study reports nothing on pesticides, pests or diseases. It shows that higher dissolved oxygen in micro-nano bubble water under SDI (with biochar) increased soil oxygen, photosynthesis, dry matter, yield, WUE and some quality indicators of cucumber. No evidence for reduced pesticide applications.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own two-season greenhouse field experiment with MNBW subsurface drip irrigation at three DO levels and biochar. Q2: Section 3.3/Fig. 6 - plant height and stem diameter increased with DO in MNBW; Section 3.4/Fig. 7 - net photosynthetic rate rose with DO (1.91-50.78% above CK); Section 3.5/Fig. 8 - total dry weight rose significantly with DO; Section 3.6/Fig. 9 - yield, IWUE and WUE rose significantly with DO concentration. Q4: Section 3.1/Fig. 3 - soil oxygen and redox potential significantly raised by DO in MNBW; Fig. 10 - these soil aeration indicators positively correlated with Pn, dry weight and yield.
rows.notes: Crop performance assessed by direct plant/yield measurement only; no second independent method. One site, soil and crop; plot-scale. No limitations stated beyond calling for more research; no SD/CI reported in text.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 - own two-season greenhouse experiment with soil aeration, moisture, temperature and EC monitoring under MNBW subsurface drip irrigation. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 3 - DO concentration in MNBW significantly raised soil oxygen content and soil redox potential (P<0.01), with interaction effects; Section 4.1 - SO increased 0.47-31.80% and SORP up to 34.74% vs CK; Conclusions - oxygen-rich MNBW greatly raised soil redox potential and oxygen content.
rows.notes: DO in MNBW had no significant effect on bulk density, porosity, aeration porosity or soil water content; the soil-condition effect of aerated drip is limited to soil oxygen and redox potential, while structural improvements came from biochar. Soil oxygen and redox potential were each measured by a single instrument; not counted as triangulation. Mechanism (bubble half-life, mass transfer) is asserted with citations, not measured. Single site/soil/crop, plot scale; no stated limitations; no dispersion statistics in text.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Figures are described by captions only, so any error bars in figures could not be verified; text reports only percentage ranges across treatments and letter groupings. The experimental design confounds the CK comparison with biochar (all non-CK treatments had biochar), but DO levels were varied within each biochar level so the aeration main effect is estimable.
